## Round table

::: {.callout-tip title="Let's go round the table — 10 minutes each"}
1. Who you are and where you work
2. **Which stock you brought** — species, area, how many years
3. What you currently use to assess it
4. What you want to walk out with on Friday
:::

::: {.notes}
Point 2 is the one that matters: note the stock, the year range and the number
of indices, because the whole week is built around their data.
:::

## This course is built around your data

Two experts, two stocks, one week.

- Presentations are **deliberately short**
- Roughly **half the day is yours** to work on your own assessment
- We are around the whole time — interrupt us

::: {.callout-warning title="What this means for you"}
By Friday the goal is not that you have seen a4a demonstrated —
it is that **your own stock has been assessed, diagnosed and reported.**
:::

## The four pillars

| Pillar | Topic | When |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **1** | Data preparation & input | Day 1 |
| **2** | Stock assessment workflow | Days 2–3 |
| **3** | Advanced diagnostics & retrospective | Day 4 |
| **4** | Reporting & presenting | Day 5 |

::: {.notes}
Pillar 2 is the heart of the course and the reason it spans two days.
:::

## The week at a glance

| Day | Focus | You will end the day with |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **1** | FLR objects & data input | Your stock as an `FLStock` + `FLIndex` |
| **2** | First fit & residuals | A default fit you can read |
| **3** | Submodel refinement | A configuration you are happy with |
| **4** | Retrospective & simulation | Evidence your model is sound |
| **5** | Reference points & reporting | An assessment report |

## Modular by design

Every module is **self-contained**. That means we can:

- **Skip** what you already know
- **Expand** what turns out to be hard
- **Reorder** if your data needs something sooner

::: {.callout-tip title="Tell us"}
If a session is too basic, too fast, or not what you need — say so
at the break. The schedule is a proposal, not a contract.
:::

::: {.notes}
Say this out loud and mean it. With two participants we can genuinely
re-plan overnight.
:::


## Materials

Everything lives in the course folder, one folder per module:

```
course/
  day01/  M1.0_welcome, M1.1_flr_intro, ...
  day02/  ...
```

Each module folder contains:

- the **presentation** (`.pdf`, yours to keep)
- a **guided hands-on script** we run together
- an **exercise script** for your own data

Reference: <https://flrproject.org/FLa4a/>

## Before we start — software check

::: {.callout-tip title="Run this now"}
Open `handson_M1.0_setup_check.R` and run it top to bottom.

It checks your R version, loads `FLCore`, `FLa4a` and `ggplotFL`,
and runs a tiny assessment to prove the whole toolchain works.
:::

If anything fails, flag it now — we fix it before Module 1.1.

::: {.notes}
Do not move on until both participants get "ALL CHECKS PASSED".
A broken FLa4a install on Day 1 costs the whole week.
:::

Then let's start with Module 1.1 — **what FLR is and why a4a lives inside it.**
